content.text: All elements of the preferred position are already present. No redline needed.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
input.rationale: Section 24 already meets our preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate (broadly defined at 1.1 on a >50% voting/management-control test) or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets, subject only to prompt notice and assignee assumption — no consent gate or Vendor discretion. 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness qualified only by assignee capability and financial standing), and may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without our consent. 24.3 does not undercut 24.1: it is expressly residual ("For other assignments"), so the mutual consent requirement reaches only transfers outside the 24.1 carve-out, and its consent standard is the favourable "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" formulation. 24.4 squarely forecloses the walk-away risk — Customer's change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service, and obliges Vendor to cooperate with administrative changes for a permitted successor. A full-text search for "change of control", "assign" and deemed-assignment language surfaced no other trigger: the only other hits are 9.2 (insolvency/general assignment for creditors, mutual, with an express carve-out that lawful reorganization is not itself grounds for termination), 26.1 (assigned personnel) and 29.2 (notice formalities), none of which create a Vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control. 13.3 tracks Section 24 correctly, permitting licence transfer to an Affiliate or successor "in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24," so the licence follows the assignment rather than lapsing. No redline required.
